children: Navratna PSU plans major fleet expansion, with over 34 vessels through petroleum-sector JVs and 51 container vessels with CONCOR and four major ports

Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), the country's largest shipping company, is expecting its profit after tax (PAT) to exceed Rs 2,000 crore in FY27, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said on Friday.

The Navratna public sector undertaking reported a standalone PAT of Rs 1,352.92 crore on operating revenue of Rs 5,778.1 crore in FY26. Sonowal said SCI had already crossed Rs 600 crore in PAT in the first quarter of the current financial year, putting it on track for a significantly higher profit this year.

“Last year the profit margin after tax was Rs 1,326 crore. This year, in the first quarter, they have already exceeded Rs 600 crore in PAT. That way in this particular financial year it is going to post more than Rs 2,000 crore in PAT,” Sonowal said on the sidelines of SCI's 65th Foundation Day celebration.
Alongside the profit target, SCI is planning a significant expansion of its fleet.

The company currently operates 58 vessels and plans to add more capacity through partnerships and joint ventures. Sonowal said SCI is working with companies in the petroleum sector to establish joint ventures, with the proceeds expected to help finance the procurement of more than 34 vessels.
SCI is also collaborating with CONCOR and four major ports to add 51 container vessels, according to the minister.
The expansion comes as India seeks to strengthen its domestic maritime and logistics capabilities and reduce dependence on overseas shipping capacity.
The government's wider maritime strategy also includes strengthening domestic container manufacturing.

Sonowal said entrepreneurs are showing interest in the Rs 10,000-crore Container Manufacturing Assistance Scheme (CMAS), announced in the FY27 Budget to support domestic production, reduce import dependence and improve the resilience of India's trade and logistics network.

“In the containers segment, particularly for container manufacturing, the Budget has created a provision of more than Rs 10,000 crore. So, that is why many more entrepreneurs are coming forward and they are showing their willingness,” Sonowal said.
He added that the government had prepared the framework for the initiative and expected the final product to emerge within a short period.
SCI Positioned For A Larger Maritime Role
SCI's fleet expansion and earnings target come against a broader push to strengthen India's maritime infrastructure and shipping capabilities.

With plans spanning petroleum-sector joint ventures, container shipping and domestic container manufacturing, the government's strategy is aimed at building greater capacity across different parts of the shipping and logistics ecosystem.

For SCI, the immediate focus is on translating its strong FY26 performance and first-quarter FY27 profit into higher annual earnings, while expanding its fleet to participate more extensively in India's growing trade and maritime requirements.
